    Office of the Commissioner of Baseball, et al v. LOC, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-caDC-24-01259 / USCOURTS-caDC-24-01259-0

    FAPD-AI: The Office of the Commissioner of Baseball and Public Broadcasting Service appealed a Copyright Royalty Board determination allocating 2014-2017 cable retransmission royalties among six competing claimant groups. The Board evaluated two valuation methodologies—regression analysis and constant-sum surveys—and concluded they should be equally weighted in calculating the relative marketplace value of competing programming categories. The Court of Appeals rejected nearly all of the appellants' challenges but vacated the determination and remanded, finding that while the Board's evaluation of the two methodologies was reasonable, the Board failed to explain how it merged those results to calculate the final allocation percentages among each claimant group. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 22:01:45 Eastern time ET
    Bultemeyer V. Centurylink, INC. (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca9-24-6413 / USCOURTS-ca9-24-6413-0

    FAPD-AI: Lydia Bultemeyer filed a class action suit against CenturyLink under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, alleging the company unlawfully pulled her credit report after she completed step four of a five-step online ordering process but before she submitted her order at step five. CenturyLink asserted a Safeco defense, arguing that even if its interpretation of "initiated" a business transaction was erroneous, it was not objectively unreasonable and therefore not willful. The Ninth Circuit reversed the jury verdict of $28 million in statutory damages and $112 million in punitive damages, holding that CenturyLink was entitled to judgment as a matter of law because its reading of the Fair Credit Reporting Act had foundation in the statutory text and no court of appeals or authoritative guidance had warned against that construction. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 22:01:43 Eastern time ET
    In re: Francis Joseph (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-26-02772 / USCOURTS-ca3-26-02772-0

    FAPD-AI: Joseph, an Indian national convicted of theft and wire fraud, challenged his ICE detention through habeas petition after completing his federal sentence. The district court granted the habeas writ and ordered a constitutionally adequate bond hearing or release. Joseph's subsequent mandamus petition became moot when the district court granted his motion to enforce the habeas judgment while the petition was pending. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 22:01:43 Eastern time ET
    Steven J. Hecke v. Commissioner of the Indiana State Police, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca7-25-03071 / USCOURTS-ca7-25-03071-0

    FAPD-AI: Steven Hecke, a federal prisoner, sued Sergeant Jeremy Brice and the Commissioner of Indiana State Police under 42 U.S.C. § 1983, claiming they conducted a warrantless search of his cell phone after his 2020 arrest on drug trafficking charges. The district court granted summary judgment in favor of the defendants based on qualified immunity, finding that no clearly established law prohibited Brice from relying on another officer's attestation that legal authority existed for the search. The Seventh Circuit affirmed, holding that neither the Supreme Court's decision in Riley v. California nor any other precedent clearly established that a forensic examiner must independently verify the validity of a warrant before searching an electronic device. USCOURTS-SEL-01

      FAPD-AI: Robert Jackson was convicted of conspiracy to distribute fentanyl, distribution of fentanyl resulting in death, and possession with intent to distribute, in connection with the overdose death of Joseph Sturges.     Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-caDC-24-05207 / USCOURTS-caDC-24-05207-0

    FAPD-AI: Federal regulations prohibit public demonstrations on the Eastern Steps of the United States Capitol unless sponsored by a member of Congress. Presbyterian minister Patrick Mahoney challenged this restriction as a violation of the First Amendment, seeking to conduct prayer vigils and demonstrations on the Steps.     Public Broadcasting Service v. CRB, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-caDC-24-01260 / USCOURTS-caDC-24-01260-0

    FAPD-AI: The Copyright Royalty Board allocated cable retransmission royalties for 2014–2017 among copyright claimants using regression analysis and constant-sum surveys as equally weighted valuation methodologies. The Office of the Commissioner of Baseball and Public Broadcasting Service appealed, challenging the allocation as arbitrary and unsupported by the record. The court rejected most challenges but found the Board failed to explain how it merged the two methodologies to reach the final allocation percentages, and therefore vacated and remanded for further explanation. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    FAPD-AI: Barbara Linhart sued New York Life Insurance and Annuity Corporation after her husband's life insurance policy lapsed and he died, alleging the company violated California insurance law by failing to provide him a designation form permitting him to designate a third party to receive policy lapse notices. 8 AM Eastern time ET

  • Observed at 08:59:20 Eastern time ET
    115 S5438 PCS: Alaska’s Right to Produce Act 2.0 (opens in a new tab)
    Legislation · govinfo API · BILLS-119s5438pcs

    FAPD-AI: S. 5438, the Alaska's Right to Produce Act 2.0, ratifies and approves all federal authorizations, permits, biological opinions, incidental take statements, and other approvals necessary for the Coastal Plain oil and gas leasing program in Alaska. The bill prohibits the President or Secretary of the Interior from placing a moratorium on or suspending oil and gas leasing in the Coastal Plain and directs federal agencies to process and maintain related authorizations. It establishes requirements for lease management unit agreements, provides exploration incentives including rental and royalty waivers, and restricts judicial review of related agency actions except through the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit. BILLS-SEL-01

    Airworthiness Directives; Textron Aviation, Inc. (Type Certificate Previously Held by Cessna Aircraft Company) Airplanes (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION · FR-2026-09-23 / 2026-19411

    official summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2015-07-03, which applies to certain Cessna Aircraft Company (Cessna) (type certificate currently held by Textron Aviation, Inc.) (Textron) Model 402C and 414A airplanes. Since the FAA issued AD 2015-07-03, there have been additional reports of cracking and multi-site cracking in areas of engine beams that are difficult to access. This proposed AD would require repetitive inspections of the engine beam for cracks and applicable on-condition actions. This proposed AD would also add a new life-limit to affected engine beams and require replacement when engine beams reach this life-limit. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-02

    official summary: This interim final rule with comment period (IFC) codifies the Department of Health and Human Services' (HHS) authority to impose a temporary moratorium pausing the registration of agents and brokers that do not have a current Plan Year registration with the Federally-facilitated Exchanges at the time the moratorium is effective and are seeking to enter into Exchange agreements with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) to assist consumers with enrollment through the Federally-facilitated Exchange (FFE) and State-based Exchanges that use the Federal platform (SBE-FPs) (hereinafter collectively referred to as the “Federally-facilitated Exchanges”).     Air Plan Approval; North Carolina; Charlotte-Rock Hill Area Maintenance Plan for the 2008 8-Hour Ozone NAAQS (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY · FR-2026-09-23 / 2026-19495

    official summary: On February 28, 2025, the State of North Carolina, through the North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality, Division of Air Quality (NCDAQ), submitted a request for the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to approve a State Implementation Plan (SIP) revision containing the State's plan for maintaining the 2008 ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standard (NAAQS) through 2035 for the North Carolina portion of the bi-state Charlotte-Rock Hill, North Carolina-South Carolina 2008 8-hour ozone nonattainment area (the entire area is hereinafter referred to as the “bi-state Charlotte Area” and the North Carolina portion is hereinafter referred to as the “Charlotte Area”). The EPA is proposing to approve and incorporate North Carolina's second 10-year maintenance plan to maintain attainment of the 2008 8-hour ozone NAAQS in the bi-state Charlotte Area, including the 2018 and 2035 motor vehicle emission budgets (budgets) for nitrogen oxides (NO X ) and volatile organic compounds (VOC) for the Charlotte Area, into the SIP. The EPA is also notifying the public of the status of the EPA's adequacy determination for the sub-area budgets for the Charlotte Area. FR-SEL-02

    S2403 ENR: Retire through Ownership Act (opens in a new tab)
    Legislation · govinfo API · BILLS-119s2403enr

    FAPD-AI: S. 2403 amends the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 to define 'adequate consideration' for valuations of closely held stock in employee stock ownership plans. The amendment permits ESOP fiduciaries to rely on valuations from independent appraisers using methodologies from Internal Revenue Service Revenue Ruling 59-60, and clarifies that this provision does not expand the Secretary of Labor's regulatory authority beyond existing scope. The amendments apply to valuations made after the bill's date of enactment. BILLS-SEL-01

    FAPD-AI: Three amendments were submitted to S. 1582, the stablecoin regulation bill. SA 2228 provides expedited certification processes for state regulatory regimes governing digital assets. SA 2229 and SA 2230 propose the Credit Card Competition Act of 2025, which would require the Federal Reserve Board to establish regulations preventing payment card networks and large card issuers from restricting electronic credit transaction processing to exclusive networks or limiting routing options, with specified exceptions for national security risks and certain payment system models.
